intervention: Legume cover crops (e.g. vetch, clover, cowpea) in rotation or as understory
context: Arable/cropped land; especially degraded soils; temperate to semi-arid with adequate rainfall
mechanism: Biological N-fixation plus continuous root carbon inputs stimulate soil microbial biomass; root exudates and litter feed detrital food webs and support pollinator forage across seasons
metric_effects: soil organic carbon: +15-25% over 2-3 years (0.3-0.6% absolute on depleted soils)
soil microbial biomass: +20-30%
pollinator abundance: up to +30-50% with flowering covers
source: FAO (2017-2022) Voluntary Guidelines for Sustainable Soil Management; Poeplau & Don (2015) cover-crop SOC meta-analysis

intervention: Agroforestry: intercrop annual crops with N-fixing/fruit trees (e.g. pigeonpea, Gliricidia, Faidherbia in sorghum/wheat systems)
context: Semi-arid and sub-humid cropland; degraded or erosion-prone fields; smallholder or large farms
mechanism: Deep tree roots redistribute water and nutrients (hydraulic lift), reduce evaporation via partial shade, drop nutrient-rich litter; structural complexity creates habitat for birds, insects and soil biota
metric_effects: soil organic carbon: +0.3-1.0%/decade in topsoil
soil moisture conservation: +15-35% in dry spells
bird and arthropod richness: +40-100% vs monoculture
source: FAO Agroforestry guidelines; IPCC AR6 WGIII land-sector mitigation chapter

intervention: Reduced/zero tillage combined with residue retention
context: Continuously tilled cropland, most soil types; best where erosion or SOC loss is documented
mechanism: Preserves soil structure and fungal networks, reduces oxidation of soil organic matter, keeps residue cover that buffers temperature and moisture extremes
metric_effects: soil organic carbon: +5-10% in top 0-30cm over 5-10 years
water infiltration: +20-45%
soil erodibility: reduced 30-60%
source: FAO conservation agriculture guidance; Lal (2004) & meta-analyses on SOC sequestration

intervention: Field margin hedgerows, wildflower strips and riparian buffers
context: Fragmented agricultural landscapes; intensified monocultures; areas near watercourses
mechanism: Increases structural habitat diversity and connectivity; provides nesting and forage for pollinators and natural pest enemies; buffers filter nutrient/sediment runoff
metric_effects: pollinator diversity/abundance: +50-70% within 1-2 years
natural pest control services: measurably increased, reducing pesticide need
habitat connectivity: reduced fragmentation at field scale
source: IPBES (2019) Global Assessment; Kleijn et al. (2015) CAP greening evaluation

intervention: Diversify rotations: break monoculture with 3-4 crop sequences incl. legumes and deep-rooted species
context: Monoculture cereal systems (e.g. continuous wheat); soils with declining fertility and rising pest pressure
mechanism: Varied rooting depths and litter chemistries feed complementary soil biota; interrupts pest/disease cycles; legumes add biologically fixed nitrogen
metric_effects: overall soil biodiversity: +10-40% (soil fauna, microbial diversity)
yield stability: +10-20% buffer in dry/heat years
system carbon footprint: reduced via lower synthetic N input
source: IPCC AR6 WGII adaptation chapter; FAO crop diversification guidance

intervention: Restore native grassland/shrubland patches and set aside degraded fallow for natural regeneration
context: Semi-arid and dryland areas; degraded commons or marginal cropland; fragmented rangelands
mechanism: Native climax vegetation rebuilds soil aggregate stability and mycorrhizal networks; provides refuges and corridors that reconnect isolated habitat fragments
metric_effects: soil organic carbon: recovery toward 60-80% of undegraded reference
native plant richness: +20-60% over 3-10 years
habitat fragmentation: reduced patch isolation
source: IPBES Land Degradation and Restoration Assessment (2018); UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration framework

intervention: Water harvesting + infiltration structures (swales, zai pits, check dams, drip irrigation upscaling)
context: Rainfall-limited (semi-arid) cropland with seasonal drought stress
mechanism: Concentrates scarce rainfall in the root zone and recharges soil moisture, extending the growing window for plants, soil microbes and dependent fauna; reduces climate-driven mortality
metric_effects: plant water availability: +15-40% in dry years
crop and cover survival during drought: substantially increased
enables long-term SOC gains by sustaining biomass production
source: FAO water-smart agriculture; IPCC AR6 WGII water-land-climate interactions

context: Soils with very low organic matter (<1% SOC), most climates
mechanism: Direct carbon and nutrient injection; stable biochar carbon accumulates and hosts microbial habitat; organic inputs feed detrital food webs and improve nutrient cycling
metric_effects: soil organic carbon: +10-30% over 1-5 years (biochar higher, longer-lasting)
microbial biomass and diversity: +20-50%
nutrient use efficiency: +10-25%
source: FAO soil organic carbon management guidelines; Lehmann & Joseph (2015) biochar review

intervention: Integrated pest management, agri-environment schemes, and reduced biocide load
context: All farmland where pesticide overuse is documented (declining insect and bird indicators)
mechanism: Reduces direct mortality of non-target species, including pollinators, aquatic invertebrates and soil biota; allows recovery of populations that provide pest control and pollination services
metric_effects: insect diversity/abundance: recovery of 30-70% over 2-5 years
farmland bird indicator recovery in scheme areas
soil microarthropod density: +30-60%
source: IPBES Pollinators Assessment (2016); IPBES Global Assessment (2019)

intervention: Managed grazing or seasonal rest (rotational/holistic) of rangelands
context: Overgrazed grasslands and savannas with declining grass cover and soil compaction
mechanism: Allows plants to rebuild root reserves and seed banks, improves soil infiltration and microbial recovery, increases habitat heterogeneity for wildlife
metric_effects: soil organic carbon: +0.2-0.5%/decade
grassland plant diversity: +20-50%
soil infiltration and drought resilience: improved
source: IPCC AR6 WGII rangeland systems; FAO sustainable rangeland management guidance

intervention: Afforestation/reforestation with diverse native species on degraded land
context: Deforested watersheds, degraded hillsides and mining/agricultural abandonment
mechanism: Re-establishes forest cover and complex 3-D structure, accelerating soil carbon accumulation, hydrological regulation and colonisation by forest fauna
metric_effects: soil organic carbon: +20-30% over decades
rainfall retention/infiltration: improved; runoff reduced
forest species richness: long-term increase (decadal)
source: IPCC AR6 WGII ecosystem-based adaptation; FAO Global Forest Resources Assessment (2020)

intervention: Control deforestation drivers and pollution discharge; enforce buffer/protection zones
context: Frontier regions with active clearing, mining or untreated effluent
mechanism: Removes the direct drivers of habitat loss and toxicity; protecting remnant habitat is more cost-effective than restoring it later
metric_effects: habitat loss rate: immediate reduction
water/sediment quality downstream: improved
species persistence in remnants: stabilised
source: IPBES Global Assessment (2019) Drivers of biodiversity loss; IPCC AR6 WGII
